text: Vehicle Gateway Control System: High-Level Design (HLD) Document ID: VH-GW-HLD-002 Version: 2.0 Document Type: Synthetic High-Level Design Knowledge-Base Document

Section 1.2 Ground-Truth Statement. This document is completely synthetic and self-contained. It is the only source of truth for the Vehicle Gateway Control System. Any fact that is not stated in this document is not specified in this HLD. The Vehicle Gateway Control System contains exactly five primary Software Components, exactly three primary Interfaces, exactly five explicit Signals, and exactly six Port mappings. Field Value Document ID VH-GW-HLD-002 Version 2.0 System Name Vehicle Gateway Control System Document Purpose Define the high-level software architecture of the Vehicle Gateway Control System Primary Communication Protocol Controller Area Network (CAN) Secondary Communication Technology Automotive Ethernet
Section 1.4 Authoritative Sections. Section 4 is the authoritative source for signal ownership (provider and consumer). Section 7 is the authoritative source for diagnostic scope boundaries.

Section 2.1 System Overview. The Vehicle Gateway Control System is composed of exactly five primary Software Components: 1. SensorInterface 2. VehicleControlComponent 3. BrakeControlComponent 4. DiagnosticManager 5. CommunicationManager No other Software Components are defined in this HLD. The system has two functional flows: Term Meaning in this HLD Software Component An architectural unit of the system that owns ports and responsibilities Interface A named contract that groups one or more signals and defines a communication pattern Port A connection point of a Software Component. A Provided Port (PPort) provides an interface. A Required Port (RPort) requires an interface Signal A named data element contained in an interface Provider The Software Component that provides a signal Consumer The Software Component that consumes a signal Communication Protocol The transport mechanism that carries signals between Software Components The primary control flow carries VehicleSpeed, EngineSpeed, and BrakeStatus from SensorInterface through VehicleControlComponent to BrakeControlComponent. The diagnostic flow carries DiagnosticRequest and DiagnosticResponse between CommunicationManager and DiagnosticManager.

Section 2.2.1 + 2.2.2 SensorInterface; VehicleControlComponent. SensorInterface is responsible for acquiring and normalizing physical vehicle sensor information. SensorInterface provides VehicleSpeed and EngineSpeed. VehicleControlComponent processes vehicle-speed and engine-speed information and generates brake control status. VehicleControlComponent consumes VehicleSpeed and EngineSpeed. VehicleControlComponent provides BrakeStatus.

Section 2.2.3 + 2.2.4 + 2.2.5 BrakeControlComponent; DiagnosticManager; CommunicationManager. BrakeControlComponent consumes brake-related control and status information for vehicle deceleration actuation. BrakeControlComponent consumes BrakeStatus. DiagnosticManager processes diagnostic requests and generates diagnostic responses. DiagnosticManager consumes DiagnosticRequest. DiagnosticManager provides DiagnosticResponse. CommunicationManager provides communication transport services for CAN and Automotive Ethernet. CommunicationManager provides DiagnosticRequest to DiagnosticManager. CommunicationManager consumes DiagnosticResponse.

Section 3.1 Software Component List. No. Software Component Role Summary 1 SensorInterface Acquires and normalizes physical vehicle sensor information SensorInterface is a Software Component. It is not an Interface. The Software Component name SensorInterface must not be confused with the three Interfaces defined in Section 4.

section_title: Port Mapping; Port Statements per Software Component
section: 3.2 + 3.3 Port Mapping; Port Statements per Software Component
text: Section 3.2 + 3.3 Port Mapping; Port Statements per Software Component. The Vehicle Gateway Control System defines exactly six ports. The mapping below is complete. SensorInterface owns one port: VehicleDataOut, a Provided Port (PPort) of VehicleDataInterface. VehicleControlComponent owns two ports: VehicleDataIn, a Required Port (RPort) of VehicleDataInterface, and BrakeStatusOut, a Provided Port (PPort) of BrakeStatusInterface. BrakeControlComponent owns one port: BrakeStatusIn, a Required Port (RPort) of BrakeStatusInterface. CommunicationManager owns one port: DiagnosticIn, a Required Port (RPort) of DiagnosticInterface.

Section 3.4 Port Connections. VehicleDataOut of SensorInterface is connected to VehicleDataIn of VehicleControlComponent through VehicleDataInterface. BrakeStatusOut of VehicleControlComponent is connected to BrakeStatusIn of BrakeControlComponent through BrakeStatusInterface. DiagnosticOut of DiagnosticManager is connected to DiagnosticIn of CommunicationManager through DiagnosticInterface. The HLD defines no additional port for DiagnosticRequest. The six ports in Section 3.2 are the complete port set.

Section 4.1 + 4.1.1 + 4.1.2 Interface Definitions; VehicleDataInterface; BrakeStatusInterface. The Vehicle Gateway Control System defines exactly three primary Interfaces. VehicleDataInterface uses the Sender-Receiver communication pattern. VehicleDataInterface contains the signals VehicleSpeed and EngineSpeed. VehicleSpeed is contained in VehicleDataInterface. EngineSpeed is contained in VehicleDataInterface. BrakeStatusInterface uses the Sender-Receiver communication pattern. BrakeStatusInterface contains the signal BrakeStatus. Interface Communication Pattern Contained Signals VehicleDataInterface Sender-Receiver VehicleSpeed, EngineSpeed BrakeStatusInterface Sender-Receiver BrakeStatus DiagnosticInterface Client-Server / Sender- Receiver hybrid DiagnosticRequest, DiagnosticResponse

Section 5.1 Primary Protocol: Controller Area Network (CAN). Controller Area Network (CAN) is the primary communication protocol of the Vehicle Gateway Control System. CAN is the primary communication protocol for all five explicit HLD signals: VehicleSpeed EngineSpeed BrakeStatus DiagnosticRequest DiagnosticResponse CAN is the primary transport mechanism for VehicleSpeed. CAN is the primary transport mechanism for EngineSpeed. CAN is the primary transport mechanism for BrakeStatus. CAN is the primary transport mechanism for DiagnosticRequest. CAN is the primary transport mechanism for DiagnosticResponse.

Section 5.2 Secondary Technology: Automotive Ethernet. Automotive Ethernet is the secondary communication technology of the Vehicle Gateway Control System. Automotive Ethernet is used for: Software Component Signals Provided Signals Consumed SensorInterface VehicleSpeed, EngineSpeed None VehicleControlComponent BrakeStatus VehicleSpeed, EngineSpeed BrakeControlComponent None BrakeStatus DiagnosticManager DiagnosticResponse DiagnosticRequest CommunicationManager DiagnosticRequest DiagnosticResponse high-bandwidth service-oriented communication calibration engineering flashing Automotive Ethernet is not the primary transport mechanism for any of the five explicit HLD signals.

section: 5.3 + 5.5 Role of CommunicationManager; Out-of-Scope Communication Details
text: Section 5.3 + 5.5 Role of CommunicationManager; Out-of-Scope Communication Details. CommunicationManager provides communication transport services for CAN and Automotive Ethernet. CommunicationManager is a Software Component. CAN and Automotive Ethernet are Communication Protocols or technologies, not Software Components. The following are not specified in this HLD: Ethernet frame layouts IP addresses VLAN assignments SOME/IP service IDs CAN message identifiers and signal encodings The SOME/IP service ID is not specified in this HLD. Section 6.1 Primary Control Data Flow. The primary control flow is: SensorInterface → VehicleSpeed / EngineSpeed → VehicleControlComponent → BrakeStatus → BrakeControlComponent 1. SensorInterface acquires and normalizes vehicle sensor information. 2. SensorInterface provides VehicleSpeed and EngineSpeed to VehicleControlComponent through VehicleDataInterface. 3. VehicleControlComponent consumes VehicleSpeed and EngineSpeed. 4. VehicleControlComponent calculates vehicle control state. 5. VehicleControlComponent provides BrakeStatus to BrakeControlComponent through BrakeStatusInterface. 6. BrakeControlComponent consumes BrakeStatus for vehicle deceleration actuation. CAN is the primary communication protocol for VehicleSpeed, EngineSpeed, and BrakeStatus.

Section 6.2 Diagnostic Data Flow. The diagnostic flow is: CommunicationManager → DiagnosticRequest → DiagnosticManager → DiagnosticResponse → CommunicationManager 1. CommunicationManager receives an external diagnostic request. 2. CommunicationManager provides DiagnosticRequest to DiagnosticManager through DiagnosticInterface. 3. DiagnosticManager processes the request. 4. DiagnosticManager provides DiagnosticResponse to CommunicationManager through DiagnosticInterface. 5. CommunicationManager consumes DiagnosticResponse and performs transport of the response. CAN is the primary communication protocol for DiagnosticRequest and DiagnosticResponse.
Section 6.3 Dependency Summary. The dependency direction in the Provides To column and the Depends On column is derived from Section 4.3. Section 4.3 remains authoritative.

section_title: Diagnostic Architecture and Explicit Out-of-Scope Boundary; Diagnostic Architecture
section: 7 + 7.1 Diagnostic Architecture and Explicit Out-of-Scope Boundary; Diagnostic Architecture
text: Section 7 + 7.1 Diagnostic Architecture and Explicit Out-of-Scope Boundary; Diagnostic Architecture. This section is the authoritative source for diagnostic scope boundaries in VH-GW- HLD-002. The diagnostic architecture uses two Software Components: DiagnosticManager processes diagnostic requests and generates diagnostic responses. CommunicationManager receives external diagnostic requests and transports diagnostic responses. The two Software Components communicate through DiagnosticInterface. DiagnosticInterface uses a Client-Server / Sender-Receiver hybrid communication pattern and contains DiagnosticRequest and DiagnosticResponse. CommunicationManager provides DiagnosticRequest to DiagnosticManager. DiagnosticManager provides DiagnosticResponse to CommunicationManager. No additional diagnostic components are defined in this HLD.

Section 7.2 Diagnostic Protocol and Transport.
